body.heading: Ears in charge
paragraphs: On this walk, your ears are the boss. Walk slowly with your adult and listen harder than you ever have before.
Every place has a sound mix. Birds, wind, leaves, distant cars, a dog barking, your own footsteps — count each different sound.

body.heading: Stop and count
paragraphs: Every few minutes, stop somewhere safe and stand perfectly still for twenty seconds. How many sounds can you count in the quiet?
Some sounds only appear when you stop: a bee humming, water dripping, a flag flapping. Moving feet hide the little sounds.

body.heading: Near and far
paragraphs: Sort your sounds into near sounds and far sounds. A faraway train and a close-up crunch of gravel live in the same walk.
Back home, your list is a picture of your place — painted in sound instead of colour.

takeaway: A listening walk shows that every place has its own music, if you walk slowly enough to hear it.
materials: A quiet route chosen by an adult
safetyNotes: Stay with your adult and stay aware of traffic — stop and stand still in a safe place to listen, never in the road.
screenFreeExtension: Draw a sound map of your walk, marking where each sound lives.
